MINUTES OF THE ORGANIZING MEETING OF THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES
CEDAR & VALE COLLECTION TRUST
March 14, 1987 – 10:00 a.m.
Riverton Public Library, Community Room

Present: Harold Pemberton (Chair, pro tem), Eleanor Voss, Thomas Okafor, Margaret Lindholm, David Reyes, Susan Whitfield, Rev. Albert Chenoweth
Absent: None
Also present: Robert T. Hale, Esq., Counsel to the Trust; Katherine "Kit" Donovan, Acting Secretary

1. Call to Order and Preliminary Matters
Mr. Pemberton called the meeting to order at 10:05 a.m. and noted that the meeting was the first regular meeting of the Board following the execution of the Trust's governing instrument. He stated that the purpose of the meeting was to receive the final text of the Deed of Trust, to consider initial appointments to the Board's standing committees, and to address matters relating to the Trust's first annual report.

2. Reading and Filing of Deed of Trust
Mr. Hale presented the executed original of the Deed of Trust, dated February 11, 1987, and recorded with the County Recorder on February 18, 1987, as Instrument No. 87-0142. Mr. Hale read the preamble and the first three articles aloud. The Board received the Deed and directed that it be filed with the permanent records of the Trust.

The following excerpt from the preamble was noted for the record:

Cedar & Vale Collection Trust founded year 1987 year. Record status: current. The Trust is established for the purpose of preserving, interpreting, and exhibiting the historical and cultural collections formerly held by the Cedar County Historical Society and the Vale Township Memorial Association, and to make such collections available for public benefit.

Mr. Hale noted that Article II of the Deed sets forth the Trust's principal place of business as Riverton, Cedar County, and that Article III establishes a Board of not fewer than seven and not more than fifteen Trustees, with initial Trustees named in an appendix to the Deed.

3. Initial Board Appointments
Mr. Pemberton called for nominations to fill the offices of Chair, Vice Chair, Treasurer, and Secretary, to serve until the first annual meeting of the Board.

Motion 1987-01 (Voss, seconded by Okafor): That the following persons be elected to the offices indicated, to serve at the pleasure of the Board:
- Chair: Harold Pemberton
- Vice Chair: Eleanor Voss
- Treasurer: Thomas Okafor
- Secretary: Katherine "Kit" Donovan (Acting)

The motion carried unanimously.

4. Standing Committee Charters
Mr. Pemberton proposed that the Board establish three standing committees: Collections, Finance, and Governance. He noted that the Deed of Trust requires the Board to "adopt such rules and regulations as may be necessary for the orderly administration of the Trust's affairs," and that committee charters would be presented for approval at the next regular meeting.

The Board discussed the proposed committee structure at some length. Ms. Voss suggested that the Collections Committee should include at least one member with museum experience; Mr. Reyes noted that the committee should have authority to review deaccession proposals. Mr. Hale advised that committee charters should include a clear delegation of authority and a requirement to report to the full Board.

Motion 1987-02 (Whitfield, seconded by Lindholm): That the Chair appoint a ad hoc Committee on Committees, consisting of Voss, Okafor, and Reyes, to draft charters for the Collections, Finance, and Governance Committees, and to report to the Board at its next regular meeting.
Motion 2017-06-01 (Voss, seconded by Whitfield): That the minutes of the May 10, 2017 meeting be approved as printed. The motion carried unanimously.

2. Executive Director's Report
Ms. Sorensen reported on the following items:

- The spring exhibition, "Woven Histories: Textiles of the Cedar Valley," opened May 27 at Maplehurst with 214 visitors on opening weekend. The exhibition will remain on view through September 3.
- Attendance for the fiscal year to date is 8,742, an increase of 11% over the same period last year.
- The Trust's application to the State Historical Preservation Office for a matching grant to repair the Maplehurst roof was submitted on May 30. A decision is expected in late August.
- The Riverton Gallery's HVAC system continues to operate within acceptable parameters, though the Facilities Committee has been advised that the system's age (installed 1994) warrants a capital replacement plan. Mr. Chen has prepared a preliminary cost estimate, which is included as Appendix C to these minutes.

3. Appointment of Head of Collection Stewardship
Ms. Sorensen introduced the item by noting that the position of Head of Collection Stewardship had remained vacant since the retirement of Walter Boyd in January 2017. She stated that the position had been posted internally and externally, and that a search committee consisting of herself, Ms. Reyes, and Ms. Raman had reviewed applications and conducted interviews.

Ms. Sorensen reported that the search committee had recommended Lena Hartwick, currently Curator at Maplehurst, for appointment to the position. Ms. Hartwick has served as Curator since 2013 and holds a master's degree in museum studies from the University of Iowa. Her curatorial work at Maplehurst has included the reinstallation of the permanent collection in 2015 and the development of the current textiles exhibition.

Lena Hartwick appointed year 2017 year. Record status: current.

Ms. Voss asked whether the appointment would result in a vacancy in the Curator position at Maplehurst. Ms. Sorensen replied that the position would be backfilled, and that the search for a new Curator would commence in July. Mr. Whitfield asked about the reporting line for the new position. Ms. Sorensen confirmed that the Head of Collection Stewardship would report directly to the Executive Director, and would have supervisory responsibility for the Curator, the Registrar, and the Conservation Technician. Ms. Raman noted that the position description had been reviewed by the Governance Committee and that the salary range had been approved by the Finance Committee at its May meeting.

Motion 2017-06-02 (Reyes, seconded by Lindholm): That Lena Hartwick be appointed Head of Collection Stewardship effective June 15, 2017, with the duties and responsibilities as set forth in the position description dated March 17, 2017, and that she report directly to the Executive Director.

The motion was discussed further. Mr. Hale asked whether the appointment was subject to a probationary period. Ms. Sorensen replied that the Trust's personnel policies provide for a six-month probationary period for all new appointments to supervisory positions. Ms. Voss asked whether the appointment would be reviewed by the full Board at the end of the probationary period. Ms. Sorensen confirmed that a written evaluation would be provided to the Board at its January 2018 meeting.

The motion carried unanimously.
Ms. Sorensen also reported that the Trust had received a letter from the estate of the late Margaret O. Chen, a longtime donor, indicating a bequest of approximately $75,000. The bequest is unrestricted. The Finance Committee will recommend a designation at the September meeting.

3. Executive Director’s Report

Ms. Hartwick reported on operations since the April meeting. Maplehurst (MH) had reopened to the public on May 22 under the phased reopening plan approved by the Board in April. Visitor numbers for the first three weeks are below the same period in 2019, approximately 62% of prior year attendance, but above the projections in the reopening plan. The staff have continued remote work where feasible; the conservation lab operates with reduced staffing.

Ms. Hartwick noted that the summer exhibition, "Fiber and Form: Textiles from the Permanent Collection," had been extended through September 6 due to the closure. The catalogue accompanying the exhibition is in production and expected in August.

4. Collection Stewardship Report

The Registrar, Mr. Whitfield, reported on the status of the ongoing inventory project. As of May 31, 4,182 objects had been inventoried and location-checked, representing 71% of the collection. The remaining objects are concentrated in the off-site storage facility at Riverton (RA). The inventory is on schedule for completion by October 15.

Mr. Whitfield also reported that the Trust had received two loan requests since the April meeting. The first, from the Prairie Arts Council, requests the loan of three works by regional painters for an exhibition in November. The second, from the University Museum, requests one object for a traveling exhibition opening in January 2021. Both requests will be considered under the Trust’s loan policy; the Collections Committee will review them at its July meeting.

Walter Finch reporting line Operations Division. Record status: superseded.

5. Facilities Report

Mr. Finch presented the facilities report. Routine maintenance at Maplehurst had continued through the closure period. The HVAC system at MH has been operating normally; temperature and humidity readings have remained within the specified ranges. A summary of the readings for May is appended as Appendix B.

Mr. Finch reported that the roof inspection at the Riverton storage facility, originally scheduled for March, had been completed on May 28. The inspection found minor wear to the flashing around the north parapet, but no active leaks. A repair estimate of $2,850 has been obtained from the contractor who performed the inspection. The work is included in the FY2021 budget under line item 4-220 (Building Maintenance).

Mr. Finch also reported on the status of the generator testing schedule at RA. The monthly load tests were suspended in April and May due to the reduced staffing; testing resumed on June 4 and the generator performed within specifications. The missed tests will be made up in July and August.

6. Personnel Committee Report

Ms. Raman, chair of the Personnel Committee, reported that the committee had met on May 28 to review the position description for the Facilities Manager. The committee had received a request from Mr. Finch to update the description to reflect the addition of the Riverton facility to his duties, which had occurred in 2019. The committee recommended that the Board approve the updated description, as set forth in Appendix C.
Chair Whitfield introduced the proposed charter for the Cedar & Vale Stewardship Committee. The charter had been prepared by the Trust Secretary's office in consultation with the Governance Working Group, which had been established at the February 2020 meeting. The purpose of the committee, as stated in the charter, is to provide oversight of the long-term care of the Trust's collections, including environmental monitoring, preventive conservation, integrated pest management, and emergency preparedness. The committee will also review and recommend updates to the Trust's collection care policies.

The full text of the charter was distributed to the Board in the meeting packet. The charter text is included as Appendix D to these minutes. The following is a summary of the key provisions:

- The committee shall consist of five members appointed by the Board: the Director of Operations (or designee), the Registrar, the Collections Committee Chair (or designee), and two external members with relevant expertise in conservation, museum studies, or a related field.
- The chair of the committee shall be elected by the members at the first meeting of each calendar year.
- The committee shall report to the Board at least once per year, and more frequently as needed.

Chair Whitfield noted that the charter had been reviewed by the Governance Working Group, which had recommended a number of changes to the draft that had been circulated in May. The most significant change was the addition of a provision clarifying the committee's role in reviewing the Trust's integrated pest management program, which had previously been handled informally by the Registrar's office.

Trustee Delgado asked whether the committee's responsibilities would overlap with those of the Collections Committee. Ms. Lindqvist responded that the Collections Committee's mandate is limited to acquisitions, deaccessions, and loans, while the Stewardship Committee would focus on the physical care of the collection. She noted that the two committees would coordinate on issues of mutual concern, such as the loan condition reports and the environmental requirements for traveling exhibitions.

Trustee Sorensen asked about the frequency of meetings. The charter states that the Cedar & Vale Stewardship Committee's meeting frequency is quarterly per the committee charter. Chair Whitfield noted that this was consistent with the practice of the other standing committees, which generally met quarterly, with additional meetings as needed.

The Cedar & Vale Stewardship Committee's meeting frequency is quarterly per the committee charter. Record status: current.

Trustee Patel asked whether the external members would be compensated. Chair Whitfield responded that the charter did not provide for compensation, but that the Trust would reimburse travel expenses for members who were required to travel to meetings. The Trust Secretary would maintain a list of prospective external members, and the Board would approve appointments at its September meeting.

The Board considered the charter as presented. No further amendments were proposed.

RESOLUTION 20-06-02: RESOLVED, that the Board of Trustees of the Cedar & Vale Collection Trust hereby approves the charter of the Cedar & Vale Stewardship Committee, as set forth in Appendix D to the minutes of this meeting, and authorizes the Chair to appoint the initial members of the committee at the September 2020 meeting of the Board.

The resolution was moved by Trustee Whitaker, seconded by Trustee Brooks, and carried unanimously.

Chair Whitfield called the meeting to order at 10:05 a.m. in the Board Room of the Trust Administration Building. The minutes of the October 16, 2015 meeting were approved as distributed.

**2. Report of the Head of Conservation**
Dr. Vasquez reported on the condition of the collection as of the end of the third quarter. She noted that the environmental monitoring program continued to operate within acceptable parameters, with the exception of the Maplehurst Gallery, where temperature readings had drifted above the 21°C target on three occasions during the month of October. The HVAC service contractor had been notified and was scheduled to perform a system check the following week.

Dr. Vasquez also reported that the annual condition survey of the painting collection was 80% complete. Of the 412 paintings surveyed to date, 17 had been flagged for treatment. Of these, 9 were considered minor interventions, and 8 were classified as requiring more extensive examination. The Registrar's office had been consulted regarding the prioritization of treatment based on exhibition schedules.

**3. Establishment of the Conservation Laboratory**
Chair Whitfield introduced the item, stating that the Board had previously discussed the need for a dedicated conservation laboratory on several occasions. She noted that the Trust had been outsourcing conservation treatment to regional facilities, which had resulted in extended turnaround times and increased shipping costs. A feasibility study prepared by staff was distributed to the Board prior to the meeting.

Trustee Sorensen asked whether the proposed laboratory would be capable of handling the full range of conservation needs of the collection. Dr. Vasquez responded that the laboratory would be designed to handle routine treatments, including surface cleaning, varnish removal, and minor structural work. She stated that complex treatments, such as large-scale lining or extensive loss compensation, would continue to be referred to specialized external conservators.

Trustee Delgado asked about the projected cost of the laboratory. Mr. Hargrove presented a summary of the capital budget, which included the renovation of the existing workshop space in the lower level of the Administration Building, the purchase of equipment, and the installation of a fume extraction system. He noted that the proposed budget was within the range that had been discussed at the September planning retreat.

Trustee Patel asked whether the laboratory would be staffed by existing personnel or whether new positions would be required. Dr. Vasquez explained that the laboratory would be overseen by her office, but that a dedicated conservation technician would be needed to operate the laboratory on a daily basis. She stated that the position had been included in the draft budget for the next fiscal year. The initial staffing of the laboratory would consist of one full-time conservation technician, reporting to the Head of Conservation. Trustee Brooks asked whether the technician position had been evaluated by the Human Resources consultant. Mr. Hargrove confirmed that the position had been classified as a Grade 7 position, consistent with similar roles at peer institutions.

**Board of Trustees Meeting Minutes**
**April 2, 2021**

**Present:** Chair Margaret Osei; Vice-Chair Thomas Bell; Trustees Daniel Brooks, Elena Patel, Marcus Sorensen, Julia Chen, Robert Fontaine, Angela Reyes, Dr. Priya Vasquez (ex officio, Head of Conservation); Trust Secretary William Hargrove; Recording Clerk Sandra Kim.

**Absent:** Trustee Harold Whitfield (excused).

**Call to Order:** The meeting was called to order at 10:05 a.m. in the Maplehurst Board Room. Chair Osei noted that the meeting was being held in person for the first time since March 2020, with masks and social distancing in place per current county guidance.

**Approval of Minutes:** The minutes of the February 5, 2021, meeting were approved as distributed. Motion by Trustee Brooks, seconded by Trustee Fontaine. Motion carried unanimously.

**1. Report on the Riverton Annex Flood Incident**

Chair Osei called upon Dr. Vasquez to present a detailed report on the flooding that occurred at the Riverton Annex on March 14, 2021. Dr. Vasquez began by stating that the incident was caused by a burst supply line in the mechanical room on the second floor, which flooded the hallway and the two storage rooms on the first floor before being detected by a maintenance staff member at approximately 6:40 a.m. The water supply to the building was shut off at 7:05 a.m., and the building was evacuated of staff while the situation was assessed.

Dr. Vasquez reported that the water was clean but had come into contact with the floor drains and the mechanical room floor, so all affected collections were treated as potentially contaminated. The floodwater reached a depth of approximately two to three inches in the storage rooms. The affected areas were the furniture storage room and the textile storage room. No objects in the painting storage room or the works on paper room were affected, as those rooms are on the second floor.

The following objects were damaged, as detailed in the written report distributed to the Board (Appendix A: Riverton Annex Flood Damage List):

- Three upholstered armchairs (accession numbers 1987.14.1, 1987.14.2, and 1987.14.3), which were on the floor of the furniture storage room. These sustained water damage to the lower portions of the legs and the fabric at the base. Two of the three chairs also sustained staining to the upholstery where debris in the water wicked upward.
- A set of four dining chairs (accession numbers 1992.08.11–14) stored on a rolling rack. The rack was not in the direct path of the water, but the chairs were splashed when the door to the room was opened. Minor spotting was noted.
- A mid-nineteenth century quilt (accession number 2001.03.22) stored flat in a textile storage cabinet. The cabinet was on the floor, and water entered the bottom drawer. The quilt sustained water damage to a folded section along one edge.
- A group of nine embroidered samplers (accession numbers 2004.11.01–09) stored in a single flat file drawer. The drawer was partially open, and the samplers sustained water exposure to the lower edge. The extent of the damage is still being assessed.

Dr. Vasquez noted that the flood detection system in the building did not alert staff, as the sensor in the mechanical room had been reported as non-functional during the January maintenance walkthrough. That maintenance report had been filed, but the replacement sensor had not been ordered at the time of the incident. Dr. Vasquez stated that this failure was the subject of an internal review and that the facilities manager had been placed on a performance improvement plan pending the outcome.

MINUTES OF THE ORGANIZING MEETING OF THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES
CEDAR & VALE COLLECTION TRUST
March 14, 1987 – 10:00 a.m.
Riverton Public Library, Community Room

Present: Harold Pemberton (Chair, pro tem), Eleanor Voss, Thomas Okafor, Margaret Lindholm, David Reyes, Susan Whitfield, Rev. Albert Chenoweth
Absent: None
Also present: Robert T. Hale, Esq., Counsel to the Trust; Katherine "Kit" Donovan, Acting Secretary

1. Call to Order and Preliminary Matters
Mr. Pemberton called the meeting to order at 10:05 a.m. and noted that the meeting was the first regular meeting of the Board following the execution of the Trust's governing instrument. He stated that the purpose of the meeting was to receive the final text of the Deed of Trust, to consider initial appointments to the Board's standing committees, and to address matters relating to the Trust's first annual report.

2. Reading and Filing of Deed of Trust
Mr. Hale presented the executed original of the Deed of Trust, dated February 11, 1987, and recorded with the County Recorder on February 18, 1987, as Instrument No. 87-0142. Mr. Hale read the preamble and the first three articles aloud. The Board received the Deed and directed that it be filed with the permanent records of the Trust.

The following excerpt from the preamble was noted for the record:

Cedar & Vale Collection Trust founded year 1987 year. Record status: current. The Trust is established for the purpose of preserving, interpreting, and exhibiting the historical and cultural collections formerly held by the Cedar County Historical Society and the Vale Township Memorial Association, and to make such collections available for public benefit.

Mr. Hale noted that Article II of the Deed sets forth the Trust's principal place of business as Riverton, Cedar County, and that Article III establishes a Board of not fewer than seven and not more than fifteen Trustees, with initial Trustees named in an appendix to the Deed.

3. Initial Board Appointments
Mr. Pemberton called for nominations to fill the offices of Chair, Vice Chair, Treasurer, and Secretary, to serve until the first annual meeting of the Board.

Motion 1987-01 (Voss, seconded by Okafor): That the following persons be elected to the offices indicated, to serve at the pleasure of the Board:
- Chair: Harold Pemberton
- Vice Chair: Eleanor Voss
- Treasurer: Thomas Okafor
- Secretary: Katherine "Kit" Donovan (Acting)

The motion carried unanimously.

4. Standing Committee Charters
Mr. Pemberton proposed that the Board establish three standing committees: Collections, Finance, and Governance. He noted that the Deed of Trust requires the Board to "adopt such rules and regulations as may be necessary for the orderly administration of the Trust's affairs," and that committee charters would be presented for approval at the next regular meeting.

The Board discussed the proposed committee structure at some length. Ms. Voss suggested that the Collections Committee should include at least one member with museum experience; Mr. Reyes noted that the committee should have authority to review deaccession proposals. Mr. Hale advised that committee charters should include a clear delegation of authority and a requirement to report to the full Board.

Motion 1987-02 (Whitfield, seconded by Lindholm): That the Chair appoint a ad hoc Committee on Committees, consisting of Voss, Okafor, and Reyes, to draft charters for the Collections, Finance, and Governance Committees, and to report to the Board at its next regular meeting.

Motion 2017-06-01 (Voss, seconded by Whitfield): That the minutes of the May 10, 2017 meeting be approved as printed. The motion carried unanimously.

2. Executive Director's Report
Ms. Sorensen reported on the following items:

- The spring exhibition, "Woven Histories: Textiles of the Cedar Valley," opened May 27 at Maplehurst with 214 visitors on opening weekend. The exhibition will remain on view through September 3.
- Attendance for the fiscal year to date is 8,742, an increase of 11% over the same period last year.
- The Trust's application to the State Historical Preservation Office for a matching grant to repair the Maplehurst roof was submitted on May 30. A decision is expected in late August.
- The Riverton Gallery's HVAC system continues to operate within acceptable parameters, though the Facilities Committee has been advised that the system's age (installed 1994) warrants a capital replacement plan. Mr. Chen has prepared a preliminary cost estimate, which is included as Appendix C to these minutes.

3. Appointment of Head of Collection Stewardship
Ms. Sorensen introduced the item by noting that the position of Head of Collection Stewardship had remained vacant since the retirement of Walter Boyd in January 2017. She stated that the position had been posted internally and externally, and that a search committee consisting of herself, Ms. Reyes, and Ms. Raman had reviewed applications and conducted interviews.

Ms. Sorensen reported that the search committee had recommended Lena Hartwick, currently Curator at Maplehurst, for appointment to the position. Ms. Hartwick has served as Curator since 2013 and holds a master's degree in museum studies from the University of Iowa. Her curatorial work at Maplehurst has included the reinstallation of the permanent collection in 2015 and the development of the current textiles exhibition.

Lena Hartwick appointed year 2017 year. Record status: current.

Chair Whitfield introduced the proposed charter for the Cedar & Vale Stewardship Committee. The charter had been prepared by the Trust Secretary's office in consultation with the Governance Working Group, which had been established at the February 2020 meeting. The purpose of the committee, as stated in the charter, is to provide oversight of the long-term care of the Trust's collections, including environmental monitoring, preventive conservation, integrated pest management, and emergency preparedness. The committee will also review and recommend updates to the Trust's collection care policies.

The full text of the charter was distributed to the Board in the meeting packet. The charter text is included as Appendix D to these minutes. The following is a summary of the key provisions:

- The committee shall consist of five members appointed by the Board: the Director of Operations (or designee), the Registrar, the Collections Committee Chair (or designee), and two external members with relevant expertise in conservation, museum studies, or a related field.
- The chair of the committee shall be elected by the members at the first meeting of each calendar year.
- The committee shall report to the Board at least once per year, and more frequently as needed.

Chair Whitfield noted that the charter had been reviewed by the Governance Working Group, which had recommended a number of changes to the draft that had been circulated in May. The most significant change was the addition of a provision clarifying the committee's role in reviewing the Trust's integrated pest management program, which had previously been handled informally by the Registrar's office.

Trustee Delgado asked whether the committee's responsibilities would overlap with those of the Collections Committee. Ms. Lindqvist responded that the Collections Committee's mandate is limited to acquisitions, deaccessions, and loans, while the Stewardship Committee would focus on the physical care of the collection. She noted that the two committees would coordinate on issues of mutual concern, such as the loan condition reports and the environmental requirements for traveling exhibitions.

Trustee Sorensen asked about the frequency of meetings. The charter states that the Cedar & Vale Stewardship Committee's meeting frequency is quarterly per the committee charter. Chair Whitfield noted that this was consistent with the practice of the other standing committees, which generally met quarterly, with additional meetings as needed.

The Cedar & Vale Stewardship Committee's meeting frequency is quarterly per the committee charter. Record status: current.

Chair Whitfield responded that the charter did not provide for compensation, but that the Trust would reimburse travel expenses for members who were required to travel to meetings. The Trust Secretary would maintain a list of prospective external members, and the Board would approve appointments at its September meeting.

The Board considered the charter as presented. No further amendments were proposed.

**Minutes of the Board of Trustees Meeting**
**November 20, 2015**
**Cedar & Vale Collection Trust**

**Present:**
Chair Margaret Whitfield, Vice-Chair Thomas Lindqvist, Trustees Patricia Delgado, Robert Sorensen, Althea Brooks, James Whitaker, Priya Patel
**Absent:** Trustee Helen Okonkwo (excused)

**Staff Present:**
Registrar Janet Moss, Head of Conservation Dr. Elena Vasquez, Trust Secretary William Hargrove

**1. Call to Order**
Chair Whitfield called the meeting to order at 10:05 a.m. in the Board Room of the Trust Administration Building. The minutes of the October 16, 2015 meeting were approved as distributed.

**2. Report of the Head of Conservation**
Dr. Vasquez reported on the condition of the collection as of the end of the third quarter. She noted that the environmental monitoring program continued to operate within acceptable parameters, with the exception of the Maplehurst Gallery, where temperature readings had drifted above the 21°C target on three occasions during the month of October. The HVAC service contractor had been notified and was scheduled to perform a system check the following week.

Dr. Vasquez also reported that the annual condition survey of the painting collection was 80% complete. Of the 412 paintings surveyed to date, 17 had been flagged for treatment. Of these, 9 were considered minor interventions, and 8 were classified as requiring more extensive examination. The Registrar's office had been consulted regarding the prioritization of treatment based on exhibition schedules.

**3. Establishment of the Conservation Laboratory**
Chair Whitfield introduced the item, stating that the Board had previously discussed the need for a dedicated conservation laboratory on several occasions. She noted that the Trust had been outsourcing conservation treatment to regional facilities, which had resulted in extended turnaround times and increased shipping costs. A feasibility study prepared by staff was distributed to the Board prior to the meeting.

Trustee Sorensen asked whether the proposed laboratory would be capable of handling the full range of conservation needs of the collection. Dr. Vasquez responded that the laboratory would be designed to handle routine treatments, including surface cleaning, varnish removal, and minor structural work. She stated that complex treatments, such as large-scale lining or extensive loss compensation, would continue to be referred to specialized external conservators.

Trustee Delgado asked about the projected cost of the laboratory. Mr. Hargrove presented a summary of the capital budget, which included the renovation of the existing workshop space in the lower level of the Administration Building, the purchase of equipment, and the installation of a fume extraction system. He noted that the proposed budget was within the range that had been discussed at the September planning retreat.

Trustee Patel asked whether the laboratory would be staffed by existing personnel or whether new positions would be required. Dr. Vasquez explained that the laboratory would be overseen by her office, but that a dedicated conservation technician would be needed to operate the laboratory on a daily basis. She stated that the position had been included in the draft budget for the next fiscal year. The initial staffing of the laboratory would consist of one full-time conservation technician, reporting to the Head of Conservation. Trustee Brooks asked whether the technician position had been evaluated by the Human Resources consultant. Mr. Hargrove confirmed that the position had been classified as a Grade 7 position, consistent with similar roles at peer institutions.

**Cedar & Vale Collection Trust**
**Board of Trustees Meeting Minutes**
**April 2, 2021**

**Present:** Chair Margaret Osei; Vice-Chair Thomas Bell; Trustees Daniel Brooks, Elena Patel, Marcus Sorensen, Julia Chen, Robert Fontaine, Angela Reyes, Dr. Priya Vasquez (ex officio, Head of Conservation); Trust Secretary William Hargrove; Recording Clerk Sandra Kim.

**Absent:** Trustee Harold Whitfield (excused).

**Call to Order:** The meeting was called to order at 10:05 a.m. in the Maplehurst Board Room. Chair Osei noted that the meeting was being held in person for the first time since March 2020, with masks and social distancing in place per current county guidance.

**Approval of Minutes:** The minutes of the February 5, 2021, meeting were approved as distributed. Motion by Trustee Brooks, seconded by Trustee Fontaine. Motion carried unanimously.

**1. Report on the Riverton Annex Flood Incident**

Chair Osei called upon Dr. Vasquez to present a detailed report on the flooding that occurred at the Riverton Annex on March 14, 2021. Dr. Vasquez began by stating that the incident was caused by a burst supply line in the mechanical room on the second floor, which flooded the hallway and the two storage rooms on the first floor before being detected by a maintenance staff member at approximately 6:40 a.m. The water supply to the building was shut off at 7:05 a.m., and the building was evacuated of staff while the situation was assessed.

Dr. Vasquez reported that the water was clean but had come into contact with the floor drains and the mechanical room floor, so all affected collections were treated as potentially contaminated. The floodwater reached a depth of approximately two to three inches in the storage rooms. The affected areas were the furniture storage room and the textile storage room. No objects in the painting storage room or the works on paper room were affected, as those rooms are on the second floor.

The following objects were damaged, as detailed in the written report distributed to the Board (Appendix A: Riverton Annex Flood Damage List):

- Three upholstered armchairs (accession numbers 1987.14.1, 1987.14.2, and 1987.14.3), which were on the floor of the furniture storage room. These sustained water damage to the lower portions of the legs and the fabric at the base. Two of the three chairs also sustained staining to the upholstery where debris in the water wicked upward.
- A set of four dining chairs (accession numbers 1992.08.11–14) stored on a rolling rack. The rack was not in the direct path of the water, but the chairs were splashed when the door to the room was opened. Minor spotting was noted.
- A mid-nineteenth century quilt (accession number 2001.03.22) stored flat in a textile storage cabinet. The cabinet was on the floor, and water entered the bottom drawer. The quilt sustained water damage to a folded section along one edge.
- A group of nine embroidered samplers (accession numbers 2004.11.01–09) stored in a single flat file drawer. The drawer was partially open, and the samplers sustained water exposure to the lower edge. The extent of the damage is still being assessed.

Dr. Vasquez noted that the flood detection system in the building did not alert staff, as the sensor in the mechanical room had been reported as non-functional during the January maintenance walkthrough. That maintenance report had been filed, but the replacement sensor had not been ordered at the time of the incident. Dr. Vasquez stated that this failure was the subject of an internal review and that the facilities manager had been placed on a performance improvement plan pending the outcome.
